learn: The beat is the steady pulse in music, like a heartbeat.
It keeps going, even, again and again.
You can feel the beat by tapping your knees or clapping.
check: How can you feel the beat?
lessons.try: Put your hand on your chest and feel your heartbeat, then tap it on your knee.

learn: When we keep the beat, we tap at the same speed the whole time.
Listen carefully so you stay together with the music.
Musicians keep the beat so everyone plays together.
check: Why do musicians keep the beat?
What helps you stay with the music?
lessons.try: Clap along to a song you know and keep the beat steady.

learn: You can show the beat with your whole body.
March, sway, nod or pat your shoulders on the beat.
Try marching to "Yankee Doodle", an old American song.
check: Can your whole body keep the beat?
lessons.try: March around the room to the beat of a song.

learn: Some sounds are loud, like a drum or thunder.
Some sounds are soft, like a whisper or falling snow.
In music, loud and soft is called dynamics.
check: Loud and soft in music is called...
lessons.try: Say your name loudly, then softly.

learn: Musicians use Italian words for loud and soft.
Forte means loud. Piano means soft.
A piano is called that because it can play both soft and loud.
check: What does piano mean in music?
Musicians use words from which language for loud and soft?
lessons.try: Clap forte, then clap piano.

learn: Music can get louder little by little. This is called crescendo.
Music can get softer little by little. This is called decrescendo.
Changing loud and soft makes music exciting.
check: Getting louder little by little is...
Getting softer little by little is...
lessons.try: Clap starting very soft and get louder and louder.

learn: Tempo is how fast or slow music goes.
A lullaby has a slow tempo. A dance song often has a fast tempo.
The tempo can tell us how to move.
check: How fast or slow music goes
lessons.try: Walk slowly to slow music and quickly to fast music.

learn: Think of animals that move fast, like a rabbit or a mouse.
Think of animals that move slow, like a turtle or an elephant.
Music can sound like animals by changing tempo.
check: Music can sound like animals by changing...
lessons.try: Move like a turtle to slow music, then like a rabbit to fast music.

learn: Music can speed up little by little or slow down little by little.
Many songs slow down at the very end.
Musicians watch a leader so they change tempo together.
check: How do musicians change tempo together?
Can music speed up little by little?
lessons.try: Sing a song and slow down at the end.

learn: Pitch is how high or low a sound is.
A bird's chirp is high. A cow's moo is low.
Music moves up and down in pitch.
check: How high or low a sound is
lessons.try: Make a high sound like a bird and a low sound like a cow.

learn: When notes go higher, we can move our hands up.
When notes go lower, we can move our hands down.
Notes can also stay the same.
check: When notes go higher, hands go...
When notes go lower, hands go...
lessons.try: Sing "up, up, up" going higher and "down, down, down" going lower.

learn: Big instruments usually make low sounds, like a tuba or big drum.
Small instruments usually make high sounds, like a flute or a triangle.
The size helps decide the pitch.
check: Which is a big low instrument?
lessons.try: Tap a big pot and a small pot. Which is lower?

learn: You have four voices.
Your talking voice is for speaking to friends.
Your whisper voice is soft and quiet, like a secret.
check: How many voices do we learn about?
Which voice is soft like a secret?
Which voice do we use to speak to friends?
lessons.try: Say "hello" in your talking voice, then whisper it.

learn: Your calling voice is for when someone is far away, like on a playground.
Your singing voice goes up and down to make music.
Calling is loud, so we use it outside, not inside.
check: When do we use a calling voice?
Where do we use a calling voice?
lessons.try: Sing "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" in your singing voice.

learn: Drink water to keep your voice healthy.
Do not shout for a long time, it can hurt your voice.
Breathe in deep before singing a long note.
check: What helps keep your voice healthy?
Can shouting a long time hurt your voice?
lessons.try: Take a deep breath and sing one long note.

learn: Some sounds are long, like a train whistle: whoooo.
Some sounds are short, like a clap or a hop.
Music uses long and short sounds to make rhythm.
lessons.try: Say a long "mooo" and a short "pop".

learn: Words have rhythm too. Say "ap-ple" and clap two times.
"Dog" is one clap. "Ba-na-na" is three claps.
Clapping words helps us hear rhythm.
lessons.try: Clap your name. How many claps?

learn: A rest is a moment of silence in music.
Rests are part of rhythm, just like sounds.
When there is a rest, we stop and wait quietly.
check: What do we do during a rest?
lessons.try: Clap, clap, rest, clap. Do it again.

learn: You can make music by shaking, like a maraca.
You can strike, like hitting a drum. You can blow, like a recorder or flute.
You can pluck strings, like a guitar.
check: How do you play a drum?
How do you play a flute?
How do you play a guitar?
lessons.try: Find something at home you can shake to make music.

learn: Instruments come in families.
Strings have strings, like violins. Woodwinds and brass are blown, like flutes and trumpets.
Percussion are struck or shaken, like drums and tambourines.
lessons.try: Sort five instrument pictures into families.

learn: You can make an instrument at home.
Rice in a sealed bottle makes a shaker. An empty box with rubber bands makes a plucked guitar.
Ask a grown-up to help and keep small pieces away from little children.
check: Rubber bands on a box can be...
Who should help you make an instrument?
lessons.try: With a grown-up, make a shaker from a bottle and rice.

learn: Music can make us want to move.
Smooth music can make us sway. Bouncy music can make us hop.
Listen first, then move the way the music sounds.
lessons.try: Sway to smooth music and hop to bouncy music.

learn: In freeze dance, we move while the music plays.
When the music stops, we freeze like a statue.
This helps us listen closely.
check: What do we do when the music stops?
lessons.try: Play freeze dance with family.

learn: When we move to music, we stay in our own space.
We watch out for friends so nobody bumps.
Pretend you are in a bubble that must not pop.
lessons.try: Dance in your bubble without touching anyone.

learn: An echo is a sound that repeats back to you.
In an echo song, the leader sings and everyone sings it back.
Listen carefully so you echo it the same way.
check: In an echo song, who sings first?
lessons.try: A grown-up claps a short rhythm. You clap it back.

learn: Songs have parts that are the same and parts that are different.
The part that repeats is often called the chorus.
Finding the same parts helps you learn songs fast.
check: The part of a song that repeats is often called the...
Do songs have parts that repeat?
Finding the same parts helps you...
lessons.try: Sing a song and raise your hand when a part repeats.

learn: In call and response, one person sings a call and others answer with a response.
The answer can be different from the call.
Many songs from around the world use call and response.
check: Can the answer be different from the call?
Is call and response used around the world?
lessons.try: Make up a call and response with a friend.

learn: When we make music together, we take turns.
Sometimes one person plays a solo. Sometimes everyone plays together.
When it is not your turn, you listen and wait.
check: When it is not your turn, you...
When we make music together, we...
lessons.try: Play a game: take turns playing a drum beat.

learn: A conductor leads a group of musicians.
The conductor shows when to start, stop, play loud or play soft.
Watching the leader keeps everyone together.
check: Who leads a group of musicians?
lessons.try: Take turns being the conductor for your family band.

learn: A concert is when musicians share music with others.
Performers practise, then play their best.
The audience listens quietly and claps at the end.
check: What does the audience do at the end?
lessons.try: Put on a small concert for your family.
